- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward trends.
- After sharp price spikes, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — suggesting poor lag adjustment.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast, failing to account for price normalization after volatility.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- Model fails to adjust for downward momentum in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Overshoots are more common after price spikes in the middle of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits poor sensitivity to recent low prices — fails to recognize bottoming or reversal signals.
